sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface expression confirmed by flow cytometry and anti-GFP labeling of non-permeabilized cells (L1, L2); protein–protein interaction with CDH2-Myc preserved by co-IP (L3); ASTN2-dependent regulation of surface levels intact (L2).
sites.rationale: The construct is named 'ASTN1-Venus' in L2 and L3, following the standard protein–FP C-terminal fusion convention; this disambiguates between ASTN1's two extracellular termini (EC1 N-terminus at residue 22 and EC2 C-terminus at residue 1302). Residue 1302 (I) is the last residue of the canonical sequence and lies within the large extracellular domain (EC2: 398–1302), 905 residues from the TM2 boundary — well clear of any TM constraint. No specific junction residue is named in any ledger line, so the position is topology-derived from the construct name and the landmarks. Python verification confirms seq[1301]='I' and the sequence length is 1302. Full-length ASTN1-Venus expressed in cerebellar granule cells and HEK 293T cells; flow cytometry and live imaging confirmed surface trafficking; anti-GFP labeling of non-permeabilized cells confirmed extracellular display of the Venus moiety; co-IP with CDH2-Myc confirmed the tagged construct is functional.

sources.claim: Biochemical and flow cytometry experiments show that ASTN2 forms a complex with ASTN1 and regulates surface expression of ASTN1. Live imaging of Venus-tagged ASTN1 in migrating cerebellar granule cells reveals the intracellular trafficking of ASTN1-Venus, with ASTN1-Venus accumulating in the forward aspect of the leading process where new sites of adhesion will form.

literature_notes: All three ledger lines (L1, L2, L3) describe the same Venus-tagged ASTN1 construct. L1 and L3 are from the same paper (PMC6196552); L2 is from PMC2905051. The construct name 'ASTN1-Venus' (used in L2 and L3) is the standard C-terminal fusion nomenclature and resolves the two-terminus ambiguity: ASTN1 has an extracellular N-terminus at residue 22 (after signal-peptide cleavage) and an extracellular C-terminus at residue 1302, both in principle accessible. Because no ledger line independently supports an N-terminal (EC1) tag and the construct name points to C-terminal, only one site is reported. No ledger line names any internal loop insertion, any intracellular insertion, or any function-abrogating position for ASTN1.
